entry.title: [BIP Proposal] No burn, Quantum Migration Proposal, Quantum Secure Asset Verification & Escrow (QSAVE)
entry.summary:
The recent discussions surrounding SHA256 and quantum computing have led to innovative proposals for ensuring the security and longevity of cryptocurrency transactions. One such suggestion involves modifying the approach towards handling older digital coins, specifically addressing the challenges posed by potential vulnerabilities. The proposal includes instituting a mechanism where old coins can only be transferred under certain conditions, aimed at enhancing security without compromising the usability of the blockchain.
Under this new system, old coins would be locked and designated to be moved solely to a lost property office after a specified period unless verified through rigorous checks. This process would classify moving these coins as a white-hat activity, legally acknowledging and supporting the ethical hacking community's role in safeguarding digital assets. The implementation would require a consensus vote, potentially streamlining its acceptance and integration into existing frameworks within the United States.
Moreover, the proposal outlines the need for a dual authentication method for the movement of these older coins. A Zero-Knowledge (ZK) proof could validate transactions originating from an individual's seed. For significantly aged coins, additional corroborative evidence beyond the blockchain data would be necessary to authorize transactions, ensuring an extra layer of security. This locking soft fork concept aims not only to prevent unauthorized access but also facilitates a smoother transition during upgrades or migrations of blockchain protocols, thus preserving the integrity of digital transactions without necessitating the burning of old coins.
This proposal is set to be formalized in a Bitcoin Improvement Proposal (BIP), which will soon be published for wider examination and feedback from the community. The ongoing contributions to the Bitcoin Development Mailing List highlight the proactive steps being taken by developers to address emerging threats and enhance the robustness of cryptocurrency mechanisms.
